answer: Watch for graders who move as one. If several accounts score the same answers almost identically, epoch after epoch, each acting as a mirror of the others, the network should treat them as a single voice and split one vote among them. Honest graders disagree at the edges; a sybil flock lands together like sparrows on one ledge. Collapsing correlated votes means an operator who spins up fifty puppets still gets the influence of one, so faking a crowd stops paying.
